newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May natgas prices gain on weather--NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May natgas prices gain on weather--NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices again showed a monthly gain for May, boosted by recent colder-than-normal weather across much of the nation, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said in its monthly survey.
U.S. spot gas prices for May averaged $1.98 per million British thermal units, up 25 cents from April's average of $1.73 but still slightly below last May's average of $2.02, NGC said.
The largest monthly gains were in Louisiana, where prices on pipelines like Texas Gas Transmission Zone 1 rose 40 cents for the month to $2.15, about even with year-ago levels.
Most Gulf pipes were up by 25 to 35 cents for the month but remained five to 10 cents below the same year-ago month.
Prices into Columbia Gas rose 25 cents from April to $2.05, still 10 cents below last year's levels, NGC said.
Prices on Oklahoma pipes were up by 15 to 20 cents, with ANR in Custer County quoted at $1.90, up from April's $1.70 but still 10 cents below last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
